about: Main Street south, from Block Square down to the Gate Yard: what stands where, who is there, who walks it and what they say. Read by Tools/build_town_level.py (GUT_TOWN_LIST=$PWD/Tools/town_main_street.json Tools/build_town_level.sh). Places are in the map's own metres (x east, y north), from for-review/design/map-of-ashmarket.md; 'yaw' and 'facing' are compass bearings (0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west). STAGE 2: the armored truck, the shopfront, the stalls, the blue water line on its trestles, the gantry, the lamp masts, the fire drums, the lanterns and the bulbs were made in Mixar for this street (ArtSource/mixar/main_*), and so were the Five Laws and the two signs (ArtSource/mixar/street). Nothing lights the street that is not seen to burn. Change the words freely and build again.
name: Main Street
street_about: The floor of the town climbs 3 in 100 from the dam. 'street_height' is the ground at the foot of the street, and from 'from_y' north it rises.
sky_about: Where the dome the night sky is painted in is centred, how big it is, and where its own ground lies (under the lowest of the place's). Without it the dome is the cage's, and this street is outside it.
beds_about: What the street sounds like under everything, over the night every place has: kinds of sound from Tools/gut_sounds.json, each a bed that goes from one recording to another.
errand: Hide & Plate, on the west side: armor for the Gut's fighters. Needle, at the counter.
Tooth & Trigger, on the east side: Brass, at the truck.
North: Block Square.   South: the Gate Yard. Sergeant Rook, at the tally desk, has work.
walk_about: The ground that can be walked on. Each patch runs on into whatever stands along its edge (a wall, a row of containers, a fence), and that is what stops whoever walks: the builder measures every model and refuses a place where a patch ends at nothing.

walls_about: The dam is three slabs with the gate tunnel's mouth left between them, and a slab at the tunnel's far end. It is 24 m high from the foot of the street's own ground, which is why its 'raise' is less than nought.

rows_about: Containers and buses end to end. 'face' is the line their near sides stand on, 'side' the side of it they lie on, and they are spread between 'from' and 'to': each span here is the sum of its models' lengths (red 6.05 m, blue 8.30 m, bus 11.0 m) and a hand's width between them, so that no gap is left to walk at. The blue one's awning is on its own left, so 'yaw' turns it to the street. The last five rows are Block Square, seen up the street.

things_about: 'block' is what of a thing stops a walker, where that is not all of it (a shop is walked up to under its awnings). A street lamp with 'lamp' burns; without, it is one of the old town's, and dead: the old line is down, and what light there is here comes off somebody's generator or out of a drum.

bystanders_about: People standing about: so many in a stretch of ground, each looking at 'look'. They keep to the verges and the barrier; the middle of the road belongs to whoever walks it.
people_about: 'beat' is a round somebody walks: each stop is [x, y, seconds they stand there, the way they look while they do]. They go from each stop to the next and from the last back to the first. Each walks a line of their own down the road (x -2.9, -1.4, -0.4, 1.0, 2.9), so that nobody walks through anybody.

people.name: Needle
people.prompt: Talk to Needle, at Hide & Plate

lines.words: Arms up. Turn. You stand like somebody who gets hit on the left. We cut ring armor for the Gut: tire rubber for what is swung at you, road sign for what is edged. Water in hand. Nothing here goes on a slate.

answers.words: Show me what is on the counter.

lines.words: Rubber takes the weight out of a club or a chain. Sign plate turns an edge. Nothing does both. Find out who you are fighting, and then find out what they carry.

answers.words: Show me what is on the counter.

lines.words: Needle sells you the plate. I would sooner know who it is for. Come by when the line is not running, and sit. Tonight it is running.

people.name: Brass
people.prompt: Talk to Brass, at Tooth & Trigger

lines.words: Scrap, tuned or relic. Scrap is cheap because you'll be back. Relic is dear because you won't.

answers.words: What do you sell a fighter?
The truck's colors. What do they pay?

lines.words: Nothing the Gut lets through its door. Hasp racks what you fight with, and Hasp does not take mine. When you have a tag and a reason, come back and I will find you a tool.
Ten litres a fight to wear them, from Butcher rank. The offer comes to your card at the Gut. I do not chase fighters down the street.

people.name: Gate Warden
people.prompt: Talk to the Warden at the head of the yard

lines.words: Gate Yard is open until the bell. Tag where the post can read it, and keep out of the wagon lane. If it is work you are after, the sergeant is at the tally desk, down by the tunnel.

people.name: Sergeant Rook
people.prompt: Talk to Sergeant Rook, at the tally desk

lines.words: Gate Post. Tags are read here and tolls are taken here, and at the bell the gate comes down. If you were thinking of going out, you are not. Not tonight.

people.name: Lane Warden
people.prompt: Talk to the Warden on the wagon lane

lines.words: Wagon lane. Nothing on wheels comes up after dark, so I am guarding a hole. Foot lane is the other side of the barrier.
Bread's hot. Water first, then bread. That is the order everything goes in here.
If it is on the table it is for sale. If it is under the table it is sold. If it is yours, you should have kept hold of it.
Tea. It is leaves and it is hot, and that is all I will say about the leaves. A cup is a tenth of a litre. Yes, I see the joke. Everybody sees the joke.
Three dice, one cup. You fight at the Gut? Then you have had your luck for the week, and I would be robbing you. Come back when you are bored of living.
Pump water, sealed at the window. I carry it. I do not sell it and I do not lend it. Hands off the cart: that is touching the water.
Market Loop. Thirteen minutes if nobody makes it longer. Do not make it longer.
Talk to the other one. I am counting.

doors.prompt: Try the gate into Pen Lane
doors.shut: Barred from the other side. The Chainmen's carts come through here, not people.
Chain-link, wired shut. The Stacks go on behind it, dark.
The outer gate: plate and rebar, down for the night. The wicket in it is the Wardens': people come in by it until the bell, and nobody goes out.

doors.note: the way out to the Flats, which is not built: nothing sets 'gate.out' yet

doors.prompt: Look in at the Gate Post
doors.shut: The booth. A die, a hammer, a box of blank discs, and the register. A tag is thirty litres, struck while you wait, and nobody is waiting.

finds_about: What lies about to be found and picked up (E, or X): a good by the name the town knows it by, where it lies on the map, and which way it is turned. Each is there once: picked up, it is in the bag and gone from the street for good.
